guides.title: Getting Started: First Steps in the Dark
guides.summary: The habits that keep a new investigator alive long enough to learn the rest.
details_html: You arrive as one more investigator in a world that does not welcome study. A few habits will keep you alive long enough to learn the rest.
<ul>
• Open your eyes. look describes where you stand. Give it a direction, a person, an item, or a container and it will tell you more.
• Walk with care. go and a direction takes you through an exit. Mind your posture; the dead weight of a body on the floor goes nowhere.
• Know yourself. status reports your condition, skills your talents, and inventory what you carry.
• Listen to the living. talk opens a private conversation with those who dwell here. Some have only gossip; some have work, and journal keeps the account of it.
• Respect shelter. Some places are warded: the cosmic forces forbid violence there, and death cannot find you. Learn the lie of the land before you test the places that are not.
• Ask the archives. help lists every topic and help followed by a topic explains it. Press ESC for the Main Menu, where the Map, your Skills, the Catalog, and this Manual each open in a new tab.
• Leave well. rest ends your session cleanly. See resting.
Read on in movement, combat, and above all lucidity. The first keeps you upright, the second keeps you breathing, and the third keeps you yourself.

guides.title: Movement: Paths, Posture, and Pursuit
guides.summary: How to move through the world, and what holds you in place.
details_html: The world is a web of rooms joined by exits. go and a direction carries you through the exit that lies that way. look tells you which exits a room has.
Stand to walk. A seated or prone investigator goes nowhere. If you have been brought low, stand first. sit and lie are yours to use when you wish to be low, and others can see that you are.
A fight holds you. You cannot simply walk out of a struggle. flee breaks away into a nearby room, at a price, and a failed attempt costs you dearly.
Resting is broken by movement. If you had begun a vigil, stepping away ends it.

Companions. With follow you move as another moves. A creature may be followed at once; another investigator must consent. A follower is raised to their feet if need be, and is lost if they cannot keep pace.
Use look with a direction to peer along an exit before you commit to it.

guides.title: Wounds, Death, and Return
guides.summary: How the body fails, what happens when it does, and how you return.
details_html: The body keeps accounts that the mind cannot. Every blow, spell, and hazard draws down your vitality.
<ul>
• Wounded - you are hurt but able. Fight, cast, and walk as you will.
• Mortally wounded - your vitality is spent and you yet live. You cannot attack, cast, or walk until you are mended. Do not linger.
• Dead - fall further and you die.
Death here is not the end of the story. You return to the world at a place of recall, with your vitality restored, and the account continues.
Sheltered places. In some rooms the wards are strong enough that death cannot take you, and violence is forbidden altogether. Seek them out when you are weak.
Mending. Healing spells and certain items restore vitality. Use cast and use before you are in the last extremity, not after.
A mind may fail before the body does. That is a separate ruin, told of in lucidity.

guides.title: Lucidity: The Fragile Hold
guides.summary: How the mind frays, what it sees when it does, and the ways back.
details_html: The faculty of Miskatonic keep a grim axiom pinned above the reading-room door: knowledge costs. Every glimpse of what lies beneath the skin of the world is paid for by the mind that beheld it. Your lucidity is the measure of what you have left to spend.
The stages of unravelling. A sound mind sees the world as it is. As lucidity wanes you pass through thresholds, each worse than the last:
<ul>
• Uneasy - the first cracks. A room may feel wrong the moment you enter it.
• Fractured - the mind begins to invent. Things are heard and seen that are not there.
• Deranged - the invention turns constant, and cruel. Even the way forward may deceive you.
• Catatonic - the mind lets go entirely. You will need an ally to bring you back.

What wears the mind. Forbidden magic spends lucidity as a gambler spends coin, and a mind already thin may be unable to afford the spell. The horrors of the dark take their share. Nor is lucidity ever perfectly still; it drifts of its own accord.

What the unravelled mind perceives. A mind in tatters is an unreliable witness. It may hear a whisper from someone who is not there, glimpse a figure that means harm, or feel the air turn cold for no cause. These deceptions arrive by the same roads as every true thing, and nothing marks them as false. Trust what you can verify, and never assume that a thing which feels real is real.
Finding the way back.
<ul>
• A folk tonic steadies the mind when taken with use (or drink). The body will not abide a second dose too soon: a tonic taken before its time is refused, and is not wasted.

• A companion whose mind has shattered can be called back by an ally who performs ground. Do not mistake this for a small kindness; it asks the rescuer to hold still, cast nothing, and stay out of any fight while it works.
• Corruption is a different taint and answers to a different rite: cleanse.
Take stock of yourself often with status. The sane investigator is merely the one whose delusions have not yet been put to the test.

guides.title: Resting: Leaving the World Cleanly
guides.summary: How to end a session without leaving a mark on the world.
details_html: A traveler who vanishes mid-stride is treated differently by the world than one who takes their leave properly. rest is the proper way.
<ul>
• In an inn, hotel, or motel you are gone at once.
• Anywhere else you sit down and keep a short vigil. When it ends, you are gone, cleanly.
• The vigil is broken by fighting, by moving, and by casting a spell.
• The vigil is not broken by speaking, looking about, or arranging your belongings.
You cannot rest in the midst of a fight. quit and logout are other ways to leave.

guides.title: Combat: Steel, Nerve, and the Retreat
guides.summary: How fights are begun, shared, and survived.
details_html: Only creatures may be fought; other investigators are never your quarry.

Begin. attack and a name starts the fight. punch, kick, and strike are other ways of saying it; they change the telling, not the deed. You strike with what you hold in your main hand, or with bare hands if you hold nothing.

Where you cannot fight. Warded rooms forbid violence. You cannot fight while mortally wounded. A newly arrived investigator is shielded by protective energies for a time, and cannot yet begin a fight.
Each round, one deed. In a fight you act once each round, so choose well:
<ul>
• taunt draws a creature's attention onto you, testing your nerve and your fighting.
• protect covers an ally so that blows meant for them fall on you.
• assist joins a fight already begun, taking up the cause of another.
• flee breaks away into a nearby room. It may cost you your round and invite blows as you turn.
Spoils. Experience goes to whoever lands the killing blow. See skill-growth.
Fighting breaks off any rest, and a stricken investigator should mind wounds-and-death before it is too late.

guides.title: Magic: The Price of Power
guides.summary: Where spells come from, what they cost, and how to use them.
details_html: Spells are learned, not found. They come by three roads:
<ul>
• read a spellbook that holds the spell.
• teach - ask an NPC who knows the spell to instruct you.
• learn - name the spell directly, a stopgap while other teachers are wanting.

The price. Every spell draws on your reserves of magic. Spells of the Mythos also draw on your lucidity, and some need material components that are consumed in the casting. These costs are paid before the working takes hold.

The craft. spells lists what you know and spell with a name studies one closely. cast and a spell, and often a target, works it. Depending on the spell, the target may be yourself, another, a creature, or the room.
Some spells take time to work. stop abandons one mid-casting, though the attempt may cost you. Practice deepens your mastery of a spell.
You cannot cast while mortally wounded, and casting breaks off any rest. Heed lucidity: a mind already thin may be unable to afford the Mythos.

guides.title: Skill and Experience: Growing Less Frail
guides.summary: Where your talents come from and how your station in the world rises.
details_html: skills lists your talents. Your occupation gave you your strongest, and a personal interest sharpened one more. The Main Menu opens the same record on its own page.
Experience comes from two sources: landing the killing blow on a creature, and completing quests. As it accumulates, your level rises. It never falls.
Quests are tracked in your journal. Speak to those who dwell here with talk, and use quest ask to learn what they need and quest turnin to report what you have done.
Knowledge of another kind is taught by those who hold it; see magic.

guides.title: Voices, Whispers, and Gestures
guides.summary: Every way to be heard, and to be seen, and to shut out those you would rather not hear.
details_html: Speech travels as far as you send it:
<ul>
• say reaches those in your room.
• local reaches your whole sub-zone. l is a shorthand.
• global reaches every investigator on the server, once your character is experienced enough. g is a shorthand.
• whisper reaches one player, and reply answers the last who whispered to you.
• channel switches your channel, and sets which one you speak on by default.

Gesture speaks without words. emote shows an action to everyone in the room, from a set of known gestures or freely as you write it. me writes an action in the third person, shown to you for now. pose sets a description that others see when they look at you, until you change it or clear it.
Conversation with the living. talk is private, a thread between you and one who dwells here.
Silence. mute shuts a player out for yourself, for as long as you choose; unmute lifts it and mutes shows who you have silenced.
A frayed mind may hear voices that no one spoke. See lucidity.

guides.title: Companions: Parties and Pursuit
guides.summary: How to travel with others, and what is asked of them.
details_html: A lone investigator is a short story. There are two ways to travel together.

Following. follow keeps you at another's heels. A creature may be followed at once; another investigator must consent, and the request lapses if they do not answer. You may follow only one at a time. unfollow ends it, and following shows who follows whom.

Parties. party invite and a name invites a player who stands in your room; they are asked to accept or decline. Only the leader may invite, send away, or dissolve the party, and any member may party leave. A player may belong to only one party.
Parties are not remembered. If the leader departs or loses their connection, the company is dissolved.
In a fight, a companion's cause is yours to take up with assist, and their danger yours to share with protect.

guides.title: Possessions: Carrying, Wearing, and Storing
guides.summary: How to gather, wear, and keep what you find.
details_html: inventory lists what you carry and wear, and what lies inside your containers.
Gathering. pickup takes something lying in the room, by its number or part of its name. drop leaves something by its slot number.
Wearing. equip puts an item to use, in the slot it suits. unequip takes it off again. What you hold in your main hand is what you fight with.

Storing. put moves an item into a container, and get takes it out. A container must be within reach, either in the room or equipped, and must have room. Name an item by its words or its number. If several of a kind are about, tell them apart with a number, as in a second backpack.
look in and a container's name shows what it holds.
Knowing what exists. catalog lists the kinds of item known to the archives, and the Main Menu opens the same list on its own page.
For things you would rather keep safe, see banking.

guides.title: The Bank: A Box Only You Can Open
guides.summary: Safe-keeping for what you cannot carry or cannot risk.
details_html: Every investigator has a deposit box at Arkham Savings & Trust. No one else may open it.
<ul>
• You must stand in a bank to use it.
• bank lists what the box holds, each item numbered.
• deposit moves something from your inventory into the box, all of a stack or only part of it.
• withdraw takes something out, by name or by the number bank showed. Your inventory must have room.
The box holds a finite number of stacks. When it is full, it refuses deposits until you withdraw something.
Things you leave behind when you depart the tutorial are not lost; they are waiting for you in your box.

guides.title: Tonics and Draughts: Consumables
guides.summary: Items made to be used up.
details_html: Some items are made to be used up. use and an item's number or name does it. drink and quaff are the same act in other words.
What an item does depends on the item. A folk tonic steadies a wavering mind; other draughts may mend wounds.
Such remedies are not to be abused. The body will not abide a second dose too soon, and a tonic used before its time is refused and kept, not wasted.
Spellbooks are read, not used; see read and magic.
